author: Charles R. Clark
describes_date: 1905 (CHM-Date depicted), a year after the scene date; elms in full leaf
repository: Chicago History Museum, Prints and Photographs, through CARLI Digital Collections (chm_pp id 245, the PDF '38_Scrapbook Volume 2', p. 27, the thumbnail captioned i71913.tif). Prairie library image a16-chm-clark-ichi-071913-pullman-1905; the thumbnail is committed at data/sources/assets/pullman_1729_chm_clark_t1881/.
locator: The whole thumbnail: the house from the south-west across the Prairie Avenue / 18th Street crossing, looking north-east, the Prairie front lit at left and centre, the 18th Street flank in shade at right with the porte-cochere's dark west arch, parkway elms in leaf before both, the low boundary wall, a hydrant and a lamp post on the Prairie parkway, and the unpaved crossing in the foreground. The camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/chm_clark_1905.json) says how far it can be measured.

note: The nearest picture to the 1904 scene of the house, and the only one in leaf. At about 6.4 px a metre it places the big things: through its camera the Prairie front's big pedimented dormer and the round-arched lights under it stand at v 11.0-11.45, where the Detroit print's camera also puts them, about 3.2 m north of the build's; and a narrow second-storey light stands between them and the south-west corner. The north block and the portico are behind the elms.
what_it_supplies: the Prairie front's big dormer and light column, placed along the front
the south-west corner, cornice and mansard heights
the parkway elms' habit in leaf in 1905
what_it_does_not_supply: the north block, the portico and the entry (behind the trees)
